design.affected_system: multimodal evacuation, assisted transport, and emergency access network
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on evacuation and emergency-access gaps
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for evacuation and emergency-access gaps
pair hazard-aware multimodal accessibility and dependency diagnosis with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Evacuation demand, assistance eligibility, vehicle capacity, route state, and hazard timing are versioned.
Compliance, household departure, and network degradation remain observed inputs or bounded scenarios.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for evacuation and emergency-access gaps.

constraints.description: The evacuation and emergency mobility diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: emergency transportation coordinator and incident commander
design.decision_question: Which populations and critical facilities lack a verified feasible evacuation or responder-access path?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The evacuation and emergency mobility diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for evacuation and emergency-access gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: hazard-aware multimodal accessibility and dependency diagnosis
independence_key.primary_outcome: at-risk people without a verified feasible mobility plan

design.intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting evacuation and emergency-access gaps, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: at-risk people without a verified feasible mobility plan
distributional gap in at-risk people without a verified feasible mobility plan
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer individual evacuation need or willingness from area demographics.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for evacuation and emergency-access gaps passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

design.title: Diagnose evacuation and assisted-mobility gaps
transportability_risks: Hazards, vehicle ownership, disability access, road topology, trust, and compliance differ.
Registration systems may undercount people needing assistance.

family.affected_system: multimodal evacuation, assisted transport, and emergency access network
claim_boundary: Network, request, and schedule records do not establish individual travel behavior or harm.
Optimized routes and allocations are planning outputs, not dispatched or completed trips.
Design-only records do not claim current city data, implementation, compliance, or impact.
family.decision_owner: emergency transportation coordinator and incident commander
family.description: Eight decisions for mobility-needs diagnosis, clearance forecasting, network upgrades, pickup siting, vehicle allocation, evacuation schedules, failure stress, and exercise evaluation.
family.title: Evacuation and emergency mobility

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
